# Human and Avatar Modeling
## Overview
Human and Avatar Modeling extends static scene representation to handle dynamic, non-rigid subjects, specifically humans, by integrating parametric body models or deformation priors with neural radiance fields [G]. Unlike static methods that assume rigid geometry, this family solves the problem of rendering articulated bodies with moving poses and expressions from limited input views (monocular or sparse multi-view) [G]. It is distinguished from sibling methods like [Specific Model Architectures](8585-specific-model-architectures.md) by its explicit coupling of neural fields with anatomical constraints (e.g., SMPL skeletons or blendshapes) to resolve the ambiguity of non-rigid deformation [G].

## Shared principles
Builds on [Scene Representation and Architecture](11368-scene-representation-and-architecture.md) [G].

## Subtopics

### [NeRF with Per-Frame Latent Codes](12042-nerf-with-per-frame-latent-codes.md)
Extends static NeRF to dynamic human faces by conditioning the radiance field on explicit deformation parameters (blendshape coefficients) and per-frame latent codes. It is distinguished from [NeuMan](12480-neuman.md) (skeletal body deformation) and [AR-NeRF](12493-ar-nerf.md) by its use of blendshape coefficients for implicit facial control. Choose this method for high-fidelity facial reenactment from monocular video where tracking errors need compensation via latent codes.

### [Neural Body](12176-neural-body.md)
Synthesizes novel views of dynamic human avatars from sparse multi-view videos by combining NeRF with a vertex-based deformable body model (SMPL). It anchors latent variables to mesh vertices, enabling pose interpolation. Choose this method for full-body dynamic avatars where sparse multi-view input is available and skeletal deformation is preferred over dense latent fields.

### [NeuMan](12480-neuman.md)
Renders a human together with a scene from a single video by jointly optimizing a scene NeRF and a pose-driven human NeRF. It introduces a canonical space based on the Da-pose SMPL mesh to avoid volume collision and an error-correction network for details not expressed by SMPL. Choose this method for single-video human-in-scene synthesis where multi-view data is unavailable.

### Xu et al.
A method for creating relightable and animatable human avatars from sparse or monocular video [S1]. It models the avatar as MLPs predicting material properties (light visibility, albedo, roughness) and geometric properties (SDF, surface normal) in canonical space, transformed to world space via a neural deformation field [S1]. It uses a hierarchical distance query algorithm blending world-space KNN and canonical SDF distances for accurate pixel-surface intersection via sphere tracing [S1]. It extends distance field soft shadow (DFSS) computation to deformed SDFs for efficient soft shadow rendering [S1].

### ARAH Pipeline
A model to create animatable clothed human avatars with detailed geometry that generalizes to out-of-distribution poses, combining an articulated implicit surface representation (SDF) with volume rendering [S2]. It uses a novel joint root-finding algorithm to simultaneously search for the intersection with the SDF iso-surface in observation space and the correspondence in canonical space [S2]. The model consists of three canonical-space networks: a forward linear blend skinning (LBS) network $LBS_{\boldsymbol{\theta}, \boldsymbol{\eta}}$, a canonical SDF network $f_{\boldsymbol{\theta}_f}$, and a canonical color network $f_{\boldsymbol{\theta}_c}$, all trained end-to-end with photometric and regularization losses [S2]. These networks do not condition on inputs in observation space [S2].

## Background
The field emerged from the need to render dynamic humans, which standard NeRF cannot handle due to its rigid scene assumption [G]. Early works like [NeuMan](12480-neuman.md) and [Neural Body](12176-neural-body.md) introduced parametric models (SMPL) to guide deformation [G]. Facial modeling was addressed by [NeRF with Per-Frame Latent Codes](12042-nerf-with-per-frame-latent-codes.md) using blendshapes and latent codes [G]. More recent approaches like Xu et al. and ARAH focus on relighting and generalization to unseen poses using SDFs and advanced deformation fields [S1, S2].

## Sources
